I asked a couple buddies with newer TVs for suggestions, and they all though I was crazy when I told them I didn't want a smart TV and when I told them why.

Well, looks like I wasn't wrong.

In the end I opted for just a regular, 37" Sharp LCD TV. No 'smart TV' features. If I want to watch Netflix, I stream it from my computer to it. I don't need to see the weather, traffic stats, get notified of new emails, watch YouTube, use Facebook or any of that shit on my TV... I have a remote control.. I don't need to give my TV voice commands. All these features exist for no apparent reason, and if you want to watch other media sources on your TV such as YouTube, Hulu, Vimeo, etc... just buy a Roku or build a cheap media PC to connect to it.
Amazing, truly. I wonder what it would have looked like.

From E3 bullshots to post-release review embargos, is giving studios cash upfront causing game quality to slip?
What (if any) role in the recent trend of sub-par quality AAA releases do you feel the push for Pre-Orders has played?

I don't think its pre-orders directly. Companies do cost-benefit analysis on whether to delay a game or release it buggy and patch it out later, and have decided that its more efficient to release buggy but on time. General gamers don't care as much about bugs unless they're really bad, but will create a shitstorm if they have to wait a couple months to play, so the slight reduction to fan loyalty and reputation is trumped by bigger sales by releasing on time. I think it has more to do with both gamers' and publisher instance on releasing "on-time" instead of having a polished product.

For physical pre-orders, I don't think that the publisher gets the money until they ship the product, the game store holds it instead. But they do get the money when they ship, not just from pre-orders but from regular sales too, so they ship before they're ready. It has always been like this, but now many more studios are willing to risk it because the risk of releasing prematurely is much lower in the days of patching.

There are plenty of reasons not to pre-order, unless you really trust the studio not to fuck up (Nintendo), and there are a few reasons to pre-order physically, Atlus games being hard as shit to find after release for example. There is never a reason to pre-order digitally though, even discounts or bonus games/DLC aren't worth it. I don't think its causing the problems you're explaining though, they're caused more by gamers not giving a shit if the launch is buggy or shitty.
